doc.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01

title: Vincent Lepresto's job, Depression pay and Richard M. Jones
summary: Paul describes the cheap Lepresto job, Richard M. Jones taking over, and then joining Walter Johnson's band at the American Legion.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: You see? And we're taking a job for a fella called Vincent Lepresto, a Paul Barnes band. Well we played for Vincent Lepresto through 33, and we were getting three dollars a night a man, and we would play two nights a week so that we made six dollars, and strange as it sounds, that six dollars was plenty of money at that time in 33, because some people wasn't, if they could make a dollar, I'm telling you, they would do good. They had people around there and some in the bread lines, and six dollars was, I used to walk down, it actually cost us 17 cents a day for our food, and we had all we wanted to eat. We would cook together, and you know that would be about a dollar and something a week, that we would, and we had plenty to eat with that, and I'd feed other people, and then we'd have extra money aside, you know, to buy and spend with the ladies and things around there. But there was a lot of confusion there, because that job, as cheap as that job was, there was musicians was grabbing at that job as if it was a thousand dollar a week job. You wouldn't imagine that thing was going on there. And then when we got to Richard Jones, piano player, come there, he came there and he was a pretty tough fella to get on. He wanted to take over everything. And he saw the band and showed the fellas that if he had the band in charge he would take the band away, but there wasn't anything away, you know. At that time, there just wasn't nothing.
Was that the songwriter, Hermione Jones from Chicago? I mean he came from here, but he wrote things like Trouble in Mind, do you remember? Was that the same one?
What's that said his name was? Richard Jones. Yeah, Richard Jones. Yeah, that's the same Richard Jones. He had quite a name.
Did he limp a little bit? Yeah, that's right. Piano player. I didn't know he was down here. I didn't know he came back.
